clue.text: A thoroughfare or none in the Hebridean seaport

indicators.note: the words or and none are placed in the middle of the thoroughfare pair

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street, a thoroughfare
a way is a road or thoroughfare
taken as written
no means none, as in 'no money'

explanation.surface: A road, or none at all, in a Scottish island port.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A thoroughfare' supplies two separate road words, one either side, and 'in' puts the middle pair between them. The port is the main town of Lewis in the Outer Hebrides.
explanation.definitionFit: Stornoway is the chief harbour town on the Isle of Lewis, in the Outer Hebrides off Scotland.

clue.text: What sister 23 did

parts.note: the old song 'Sister Susie's sewing shirts for soldiers' says what the girl at 23 was busy doing

explanation.surface: What a sister at number 23 got up to.
explanation.walkthrough: 23 down is SUSIE; the First World War music-hall song is 'Sister Susie's Sewing Shirts for Soldiers'.
explanation.definitionFit: Past tense of stitching with needle and thread, as she did in the song.

clue.text: Varsity type shoe

explanation.surface: The kind of footwear a university student wears.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of Oxford University; and an old style of laced half-boot named after that city.

clue.text: Cleeks can be made into ornaments

indicators.note: the letters are made into something new, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Golf irons turned into jewellery.
explanation.walkthrough: A cleek is an old golf club; 'can be made into' rearranges CLEEKS CAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Chains or strings of beads worn round the throat as decoration.

clue.text: Dry up beef joints? That's the wrong way round

parts.note: to wither is to shrivel and dry up
shins are cuts of beef from the leg

explanation.surface: Drying out cuts of meat in the wrong order.
explanation.definitionFit: Means anticlockwise, against the sun's course, thought unlucky.

clue.text: Boy sent up as a raw recruit

indicators.note: in a down clue, sent up means read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A lad dispatched as a new army recruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sent up' reverses BOY; the answer began as back-slang for boy.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for a callow lout, once used of an untrained newcomer.

clue.text: Fish to clear the bottom of a ship

definitions.text: to clear the bottom of a ship

explanation.surface: A fish, and a job cleaning a hull in dry dock.
explanation.definitionFit: A freshwater fish of the carp family; and an old nautical verb for burning weed and barnacles off a hull.

clue.text: An outspoken poet?

explanation.surface: A writer of verse who speaks his mind.
explanation.definitionFit: Frank and plain-speaking; and the surname of Wilfrid Scawen, the Victorian English poet and anti-imperialist campaigner.

clue.text: Stop — amber changing to green

indicators.note: changing means altering the order of the letters

parts.note: a green light means go

explanation.surface: Traffic lights: halt, amber switching to green.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changing' rearranges AMBER into EMBAR, then GO for green.
explanation.definitionFit: A ban on trade that halts commerce with a country.

clue.text: A ship to put in charge in wartime

definitions.text: A ship to put in charge in wartime

parts.words: A ship to put in charge in wartime
parts.note: 'put in charge' suggests command, but it means placing explosive charges in the sea

explanation.surface: A vessel given to a commander during war.
explanation.definitionFit: A naval vessel that deposits explosive mines in the water.

clue.text: An impression ready for firing?

explanation.surface: A print that is ready to be fired, like a pot or a gun.
explanation.definitionFit: A print taken from a carved block is an impression; timber that has been chopped is ready to burn on the fire.

clue.text: A powerful family drink

explanation.surface: A drink favoured by a mighty dynasty.
explanation.definitionFit: The royal house that ruled France and Spain; and an American whiskey made mainly from corn.

clue.text: The stuff to give the troops?

definitions.text: The stuff to give the troops?

parts.words: The stuff to give the troops?
parts.note: the phrase usually means rations or rum, but what soldiers are put through on the parade ground is marching practice

explanation.surface: What soldiers need to keep them happy.
explanation.definitionFit: Military training in marching and handling weapons is what recruits are given daily.

clue.text: Choose the examination of this college

parts.note: to elect is to choose by vote
an oral is a spoken examination

explanation.surface: Picking the viva exam set by a particular college.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'college' is the US electoral college that chooses the President, not a university.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describing the body of delegates who formally choose the American President.

clue.text: Greatly cheered and relaxed with a hit perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps signals that the letters could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Delighted and loosened up by a success.
explanation.definitionFit: Elated, thrilled, lifted in spirits.

clue.text: One blames its carrier

parts.note: to carry the blame for others is the idiom 'carry the ...', so the blame is the thing carried

explanation.surface: Someone always blames whoever brings the bad news.
explanation.definitionFit: From the idiom of carrying the can: taking blame for others, so the tin is what the scapegoat bears.

clue.text: Discord when the Scots call a company false

parts.note: ca' is Scots for call
Co is the abbreviation for company
phony means fake or false

explanation.surface: Trouble when Scots denounce a firm as a fraud.
explanation.definitionFit: A harsh, jarring mix of sounds.

clue.text: Medical data evidenced by all those luggage labels?

definitions.text: evidenced by all those luggage labels

explanation.surface: Patient records, or the stickers on a well-travelled suitcase.
explanation.definitionFit: A patient's medical record of past illness; and the travels of a suitcase, as shown by its stickers.

clue.text: A slight quantity of mistrust

explanation.surface: Just a touch of doubt.
explanation.definitionFit: A trace or hint, as in a suggestion of garlic; and a feeling of doubt about someone's honesty.

clue.text: Food to arrive-bit less cooked ?

parts.note: to come is to arrive

indicators.note: cooked means falsified or messed about, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Food arriving a little underdone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked' is the anagram signal; the dash in the surface hides that 'arrive' and 'bit less' are separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal word for edible things, provisions.

clue.text: Love a rumba with this crazy bird

indicators.note: crazy means wild or disordered, so the letters are mixed

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, so the letter O

explanation.surface: Dancing a mad rumba with a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A large African stork, also its soft down.

clue.text: Coney, perhaps-sound suggestion too !

annotationWithheld.why: 'Coney, perhaps-sound suggestion too !': Coney (rabbit) defines FUR, but no reading of 'sound suggestion too' gives FUR as a homophone or second sense

clue.text: 19 ac intended, say, to work up

indicators.note: say signals that the words are spoken and heard

parts.note: 19 across is FUR, and intended means meant

explanation.surface: Meant, as said aloud, to stir things up.
explanation.definitionFit: To stir up trouble or excite, like yeast working.

clue.text: Show feline contentment about the hunt if he gets his money's worth ?

indicators.note: about means going round, so the hunt word sits inside the cat-sound word

parts.note: a contented cat purrs
a chase is a hunt

explanation.surface: A cat purring over the hunt as a satisfied customer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Show feline contentment' is a verb phrase giving the cat's sound, and 'about' wraps it round the hunt word.
explanation.definitionFit: A buyer is someone who pays and receives goods in return.

clue.text: Get taken for a ride ?

parts.note: not being cheated: this is getting a free lift by thumbing at the roadside

explanation.surface: Being swindled.
explanation.definitionFit: To hitchhike, travelling in strangers' cars for free.

clue.text: One medical man is highly regarded in Wales

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
Dr is the abbreviation for doctor

explanation.surface: A Welsh doctor who is greatly respected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'highly regarded' is a pun: Cader Idris is a mountain in Wales, so it is looked up at.
explanation.definitionFit: Cader Idris is a peak in Snowdonia, Wales, seen from far below.

clue.text: A special issue features this girl

indicators.note: special suggests a treated form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A girl appears in a special edition of a magazine.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl's name, short for Susan.

clue.text: Burns to escape from this path

definitions.text: Burns to escape from this path

parts.words: Burns to escape from this path
parts.note: not the poet: a spacecraft fires its engines in burns to leave the curved path it follows round a planet

explanation.surface: Robert Burns making a getaway down a track.
explanation.definitionFit: Describes the circuit a satellite follows round a planet, left only by firing its rockets.

clue.text: Beat, and bent on this licking

explanation.surface: Thrashed, eager to give a hiding.
explanation.definitionFit: To thrash; and the verb in 'lam into', to set about someone with a beating.

clue.text: The right stands to take?

parts.note: the idiom 'right as a ...' names a three-legged stand, so these are stands that are proverbially right

explanation.surface: Which stance should one adopt?
explanation.walkthrough: From the saying 'as right as a trivet', meaning perfectly sound; trivets are stands for pots.
explanation.definitionFit: Three-legged metal supports set over a fire or under a hot dish.

clue.text: Not stuff to endure, as the clown said

definitions.text: Not stuff to endure, as the clown said

parts.words: Not stuff to endure, as the clown said
parts.note: Feste the clown in Twelfth Night sings that this 'is a stuff will not endure'

explanation.surface: A jester remarks on things too bad to bear.
explanation.walkthrough: The clown is Feste, whose song in Shakespeare's Twelfth Night ends 'Youth's a stuff will not endure'.
explanation.definitionFit: Being young, which the song warns passes quickly.

clue.text: Paris worker has a small place for meals on the motorway

parts.note: the M1 is Britain's first long motorway, London to Leeds
a dinette is a small dining area

explanation.surface: A Parisian employee keeps a little eatery at a motorway services.
explanation.walkthrough: M1 is written MI, the 1 read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: A young Parisian shop girl or seamstress in the fashion trade.
